troubleshooting.symptom: System will not build pressure — pump runs but pressure stays low
steps: Check hydraulic oil level in the reservoir. Low oil will cause pump cavitation and inability to build pressure.
Check the return filter bypass indicator. A bypassed filter severely restricts flow.
Verify the directional control valve is shifting fully — a partial shift will bypass oil back to tank.
Check the system relief valve setting (should be set to 3500 PSI max). If the relief valve is stuck open, pressure cannot build.
Inspect pump coupling for wear or breakage — a broken coupling spider will cause the pump shaft to spin without engaging.
If all above check out, the pump may have worn internal components. Check for excessive heat at the pump body during operation.

troubleshooting.symptom: Motor trips overload relay during operation
steps: Allow motor to cool fully (minimum 15 minutes) before resetting the overload.
Check the overload relay trip current setting — it should be set to 110% of motor FLA (Full Load Amperes from nameplate).
Check for excessive system pressure — if the relief valve is set too high, the pump motor works harder than designed.
Inspect the motor ventilation for blockage — a clogged motor fan causes thermal overload even at rated current.
Measure actual motor current with a clamp meter during operation and compare to nameplate FLA.
If current is normal but overload still trips, the overload relay may be faulty — replace with matching amperage range unit.
